question:
A 22-year-old female PhD student presents with a one-week history of a rash on her right upper
extremity. She reports that the rash initially appeared as clustered "pimples," preceded by intense
burning pain in the affected area two days before the eruption. While the pain has diminished, the rash
persists despite application of over-the-counter zinc ointment. She works extensive hours in a
laboratory and has multiple sexual partners. Her only medication is oral contraception. Examination
reveals a temperature of 37.8°C (100.0°F), pulse of 87/min, and blood pressure of 101/74 mm Hg.
Multiple crusted lesions are observed along the medial aspect of the upper extremity from the axillary
fossa to the forearm. Neurological and other physical examinations are unremarkable. What is the
most appropriate next step in management? Answer Choices: (A) STI screening panel (B) HIV
screening (C) Acyclovir therapy (D) Culture of lesions (E) Serologic testing for syphilis (F) Topical
corticosteroid treatment (G) Reassurance and follow-up (H) Valacyclovir therapy (I) Skin biopsy (J)
Empiric antibiotic therapy
 A. Serologic testing for syphilis
B. Empiric antibiotic therapy
C. Culture of lesions
D. Topical corticosteroid treatment
E. Valacyclovir therapy
F. Skin biopsy
G. Reassurance and follow-up
H. STI screening panel
I. Acyclovir therapy

J. HIV screening
